 :JUDGMENT:
This is a Petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the death of Shivarudraiah S/o Kallaiah in the Road Traffic Accident.

sentences.text:
2. The Brief averments of the Petition are as under:
That on 04.11.2024 at about 9.15 a.m., on Kunigal- Bangalore Road, NH-75, near Government Hospital, Solur, Magadi Taluk, while Shivarudraiah (deceased) was Shivamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100165378/
2
riding the TVS Moped bearing no.KA-42-H-8517 on the left-side of the road, the KSRTC Bus bearing no.KA-13-F-2363 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against his Moped.
As a result, he fell-down, sustained severe head- injuries.
He was immediately shifted to Solur Government Hospital and then to Victoria Hospital where he succumbed to the injuries.
3. That prior to the date of accident, Shivarudraiah was hale and healthy.
he was an agriculturist and was cultivating his own land and was earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
4. That the accident is solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC bus.
Respondent being the Owner cum Internal Insurer of the bus is liable to pay the compensation to Petitioners.
Hence this petition.
5. In pursuance of service of notice, Respondent appeared through its counsel and filed objections to main petition.
6. In the Objection Statement, Respondent-KSRTC has denied the negligent driving of the driver of bus.
It is denied that the petitioners are the legal-heirs of the deceased.
It is also contended that the accident was due to the negligence of Shivarudraiah (deceased) who was riding the vehicle without valid, effective driving licence and without wearing helmet.
That Shivarudraiah was solely responsible for the alleged accident.
Respondent has thus prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

7. On the rival pleadings, the following Issues have been framed:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the Petitioner proves that he is the legal-representative of the deceased?

2. Whether the Petitioner proves that Shiva Rudraiah B.K died due to injuries sustained by her in an accident occurred on 04.11.2024 at about 9.00 a.m., on NH- 75 Kunigal-Bengaluru Road, near Govt.Hospital, Solur, Magadi Taluk due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA- 13-F-2363?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

4 . What Order or Award?
8.
The petitioner no.3 has got himself examined as PW.1 and Exs.P.1 to 18.

On the other hand,
Respondent-KSRTC examined its driver as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 to 3(a).
9.

My answer to the Issues are as under :
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Shivamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100165378/
3  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative.
 Issue No.4 : As per the Final Order,
 for the following :
 REASONS  10. Issue No.2: It is the case of Petitioners that one Shivarudraiah who is the husband of petitioner no.1, 2, and father of petitioner no.3 to 7 died in the Road Traffic Accident caused by the driver of the offending KSRTC bus bearing no. KA-13-F-2363.

sentences.text: On the other hand, the Respondent-KSRTC has denied the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the bus.
11. On behalf of petitioners, petitioner no.3 has got himself examined as PW.1 and Exs.P.1 to 18 have been marked.

Exs.P.1 to Ex.P.10 are the true copy of FIR and Complaint, Inquest Report along with Statement of witnesses, PM report, Spot Mahazar, Spot sketch, IMV report, Notice under Section 133 of M.V.Act & its Reply, Charge sheet.

12. A perusal of Exs.P.1 shows that on the complaint filed by the son of deceased Shivarudraiah, who is none other than petitioner no.3, Kudur Police have registered the case against the driver of the bus bearing no.KA-13-F-2363 for the offences punishable under Section 281, 106(1) of BNS.
As per Ex.P.1, the KSRTC Bus bearing no.KA-13-F-2363 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, has dashed against the TVS Moped of Shivarudraiah, from behind.
The Spot Sketch and Mahazar at Exs.P.5 & 6 respectively, show that the accident has occurred almost on the left-hand-side edge of the Main Road.
And in the IMV Report at Ex.P.7, the front left-side bumper of the KSRTC Bus is shown to have been scratched in the corner.

This goes to show that the accident is due to the rash & negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC Bus who has dashed against the TVS Moped of Shivarudraiah, from behind, while he was proceeding on the left-hand-side edge of the Main Road.

That the accident would not have taken-place if the KSRTC Bus driver had not be rash &
negligent.
Ex. P.3 is the inquest report along with statement of witnesses.
.Ex.P.4 is the Post Mortem Report which shows that cause of death is due to head injury sustained.
Exs . P.8
& 9 are the Notice under Section 133 of M.V.Act & its Reply.
After investigation, Police have filed the Charge-sheet at Ex.P.10 against the driver of KSRTC bus for the offences punishable under Sections 281, 106(1) of BNS.
Ex . P.11
is RTC Extract.
Exs . P.12 to 18 are the notarized-copy of Aadhar cards of petitioners.
13. Thus, the Spot Sketch at Ex.P.6 coupled with the Charge Sheet at Ex.P.10 proves the negligence on the part of the KSRTC Bus driver.

Also, the Respondent who has examined its driver as RW.1, has admitted that Shivarudraiah was riding the Motor-cycle on the left-hand-side edge of the road;
however, he has deposed that Shivarudraiah has all of a sudden taken to his right.
But this statement of RW.1 cannot be believed because he has not challenged the charge-sheet filed against him.

14. Thus having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, oral & documentary evidence on record, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is due to the rash and negligent Shivamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100165378/
4 driving of the driver of the offending-bus bearing Reg. No.KA-13-F-2363, in which Shivarudraiah has been injured and sustained injuries and has later succumbed to the same.

sentences.text: Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the 'Affirmative'.
15. Issue No.1 and 3:
Both these issues are taken-up together for discussion to avoid the repetition of the facts.
The petitioners have furnished the notarized-copy of their Aadhar cards at Exs.P.12 to 18.

The complaint at Ex.P.2 and the Statements of witness annexed to the Inquest Report at Ex.P.3 shows that deceased Shivarudraiah had two-wives - petitioner no.1, 2, and petitioner no.3 to 7 are his children.
This aspect is also admitted by PW.1 in his cross-examination.
This proves the relationship of petitioners with that of deceased Shivarudraiah.
Moreover, there is no dispute regarding the relationship.
Thus it is proved that the petitioners legal- representatives of the deceased Shivarudraiah.
16. Next, as per the petition, the deceased was aged about 75 years as on the date of accident.
The P.M.Report at Ex.P.4 as well as in all the Police documents, the age of Shivarudraiah is shown as 75 years, but no document is produced.
Hence the age of the deceased as on the date of accident is taken as 75 years.
17. Next as per the petition, Shivarudraiah was an agriculturist earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
The petitioners have produced the RTC Extract at Ex.P.11 standing in the name of Shivarudraiah, but it does prove the income.
Admittedly, all the children of Shivarudraiah who are all aged more than 39 years are married and are leading their lives independently.

Moreover, considering the age of Shivarudriah who is aged above 75 years (or may be more because no document in support his age has been produced by the petitioner) none of the petitioners can be regarded as his 'dependents'.

Hence the petitioners are no doubt the 'legal- representatives' of deceased Shivarudraiah, but in the absence of evidence that the petitioners depended on the earnings of the deceased, they cannot be considered 'his dependents'.
Under the circumstances, the petitioner is though entitled for compensation, is not entitled for compensation under the Head 'Loss of Dependency'.

18. With this background, the compensation to which the petitioners are entitled-to is discussed as under :
Here, it would be apt to the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil)
No.25590/2017 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others): wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that: 'Loss of Estate' has to be compensated by awarding Rs.15,000/-, 'Loss of Consortium' should be Rs.40,000/-
and 'Funeral Expenses' should be Rs.15,000/-".

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced @ 10% in every three years".

In the light of the above decision, petitioner no.1 & 2 who are the wives of deceased Shivarudraiah are entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/-, and petitioner no.3 to 7 who are the children of deceased Shivarudraiah are entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/-, under Shivamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100165378/
5 the head of 'Loss of Consortium' and Rupees 18,000/- towards 'Loss of Estate' and Rupees 18,000/- towards 'Funeral Expenses'.
20.
Next as per the petition, the Petitioners have spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- for shifting the dead body, for performing funeral & obsequies.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for some amount towards 'Transportation of Dead Body'.
An amount of Rs.10,000/- under this Head would be just and reasonable.

21. TOTAL QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
1. Loss of Consortium Rs. 88,000/-
2. Loss of Estate Rs. 18,000/-
3. Funeral Expenses Rs. 18,000/-
4. Transportation of Dead Body Rs. 10,000/-
Out of the aforesaid total compensation, Rs.25,000/- is to be deducted towards the interim-compensation already paid by respondent-KSRTC to the petitioners.
Thus in all, the Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.1,09,000/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.

Petitioner No.1 being the first-wife is entitled to 40%, petitioner No.2 being the second-wife is entitled to 35% and petitioner No.3 to 7 are entitled to 5% each out of the total compensation awarded.
22. Regarding Liability : As already discussed above, the petitioners have proved that the accident is due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing no.KA-13- F-2363.
Therefore, Respondent being the Owner and Internal Insurer is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners with interest.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative' and Issue No.3 'Partly in the Affirmative".
23. Issue No.4 : In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The Claim Petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.1,09,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of Award Shivamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100165378/
6 amount.
The Respondent is liable to pay the  compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 30 days from the date of the Award.
Petitioner no.1 is entitled to 40% of the total compensation awarded.

After deposit,
the entire amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner no.1 by way of E-payment on proper identification.
Petitioner no.2 is entitled to 35% of the total compensation awarded.

After deposit,
the entire amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner no.2 by way of E-payment on proper identification.
Petitioner no.3 to 7 are entitled to 5% each of the total compensation awarded.
After deposit, the entire amount awarded to petitioner no.3 to 7 is ordered to be released in their favour by way of E-payment on proper- identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.

21. TOTAL QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
1. Loss of Consortium Rs. 88,000/-

Out of the aforesaid total compensation, Rs.25,000/- is to be deducted towards the interim-compensation already paid by respondent-KSRTC to the petitioners.
Thus in all, the Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.1,09,000/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.

Petitioner No.1 being the first-wife is entitled to 40%, petitioner No.2 being the second-wife is entitled to 35% and petitioner No.3 to 7 are entitled to 5% each out of the total compensation awarded.
Therefore, Respondent being the Owner and Internal Insurer is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners with interest.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative' and Issue No.3 'Partly in the Affirmative".
